title: Efficient passive initialization of a three-dimensional quantum memory
statement: For the main three-dimensional stabilizer-memory family with random embedding of Balasubramanian, Davydova and Lin, can the logical-zero thermal state |0><0|_L tensor rho_beta be initialized efficiently from an accessible state by the within-sector thermalization route in Section 1.3? Specify allowed initial controls, bath dynamics, temperature, preparation error, logical error and system-size scaling.
source_locator: Balasubramanian, Davydova and Lin, Section 1.3, item 2; later classical result, abstract and Section 1.
status_basis: Section 1.3 explicitly leaves efficient initialization untreated. The later two-dimensional classical stability result addresses a different task. A focused search found no solution for the stated quantum construction; this is not an exhaustive status determination.
plain_summary: A memory is useful only if information can be loaded into its protected state. This asks whether the proposed passive memory can be initialized without preparation taking prohibitively long.
assumptions: Use the main random-embedding family in Sections 1.2.2 and 3, with the storage analysis in Section 5, and its thermal encoding. Specify the construction parameters and any probability statement over embeddings.
Declare the bath dynamics and nonzero temperature regime before a quantitative claim.

Approach the thermal syndrome state while bounding logical errors during preparation. Exact conservation of a logical sector is not assumed; global equilibration that loses the stored information is not success.
scope: The logical-zero preparation route explicitly discussed in the source. The open direction does not prescribe a unique efficiency threshold. Define input preparation, allowed controls and an error metric before an attempt; preparing arbitrary unknown logical states is a further claim.
target: Establish an efficient preparation procedure under explicit conditions, or prove a preparation bottleneck for a specified admissible procedure.
success_criteria: Identify the preparation channel, its admissible initial states and the target thermal syndrome state.
Give a rigorous accuracy bound with explicit dependence on system size, temperature and tolerance.
Bound logical errors during preparation and compare the initialization time with the storage regime. Do not replace metastable protection by an assumed exactly conserved logical sector.
Limit any obstruction to the protocols and parameter regime actually proved.
known_results: The source reports a storage theorem for its main random-embedding construction using thermal encoding. Efficient initialization is left open.
Its suggested within-sector route may encounter energetic bottlenecks; a cited rapid-initialization argument has an unmet LDPC metacheck assumption.
The October follow-up treats two-dimensional classical stability, not this initialization problem.

The separate explicit-embedding construction in Sections 1.2.4 and 6 does not yet have the complete exponential-lifetime proof in this paper; its preparation cannot simply inherit the main construction's guarantee.
prerequisites: Stabilizer codes, syndrome sectors and Gibbs states.
Local thermal dynamics, mixing estimates and asymptotic error bounds.
significance: Initialization connects a theoretical storage construction to a usable information-processing procedure. A rigorous obstruction would also clarify what the construction requires.

requirements.compute: Unmeasured. Small instances can test definitions, while exact state-space simulation grows rapidly. Analytical bounds may avoid full simulation; no affordable full-scale run is promised.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Ideal stabilizer interactions, chosen thermal dynamics and a stated logical-sector encoding. Hardware robustness is a separate claim.

methods: Analyze the source's proposed within-sector thermalization route.
Check the assumptions of applicable mixing and preparation theorems before transferring them.
obstacles: A lifetime bound does not supply an initialization bound.
Mixing across logical sectors destroys the desired information.
A good finite-size simulation need not imply efficient asymptotic preparation.

steps: State the physical or mathematical controls allowed during preparation.
Match the Hamiltonian, encoding and bath to the cited construction.
Check the logical-zero target and quantify leakage or logical errors rather than imposing perfect within-sector conservation without justification.
Audit every size-dependent constant, accuracy estimate and temperature restriction.
Treat simulations as diagnostics and obtain specialist review of the final asymptotic argument.
validation.human_review_difficulty: High: the protocol must fit the code construction while its error and resource estimates remain uniform in the declared limit.
validation.statement_alignment: Ground-space encoding, mixed thermal encoding, active preparation and passive within-sector relaxation are distinct tasks.

known_attempts: The original outlook proposes a possible preparation route and describes obstacles; no project attempt has been run.
unresolved_checks: Choose a precise efficiency target and permitted controls.
Audit dependencies in the memory theorem before using them.
Search for subsequent initialization results and compare their models.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: A theorem applies only to its stated Hamiltonian and dynamics. Source inspection is not independent validation of the construction.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: No experimental device, fabrication tolerance or measured memory performance is established by this entry.
